name: Scrapper
body:
Scrapper
CR 1/2

This 6-legged, furry creatures scuttles toward you, saliva dripping from its mouth.

XP 200
N Tiny magical beast
Init +2; Senses darkvision 60 ft., low-light vision, scent; Perception +2

DEFENSE

AC 15, touch 14, flat-footed 13 (+2 Dex, +1 natural, +2 size)
hp 7 (1d10+2)
Fort +6, Ref +4, Will +2

OFFENSE

Speed 30 ft., climb 30 ft.
Melee 4 claws +3 (1d2), bite +3 (1d3)
Space 2-1/2 ft.; Reach 0 ft.

STATISTICS

Str 11, Dex 15, Con 14, Int 2, Wis 14, Cha 7
Base Atk +1; CMB -1; CMD 9 (17 vs. trip)
Feats Great Fortitude Skills Climb +12

SPECIAL ABILITIES

Antiseptic Saliva (Ex)

Scrappers are never at risk of contracting a disease through food. A scrapper can, as a full-round action, lick clean an injury that’s not older than 1 minute. If the licked creature has contracted a disease through this injury (a ghoul’s bite, for example), it can attempt a second saving throw against the disease with a +4 bonus. If the creature succeeds at this save, it is treated as if it made the original save.

ECOLOGY

Environment any
Organization solitary, pair
Treasure incidental

Scrappers are hardy creatures, named as much for their typical diet as for their occasionally fierce behavior. The most unique and perhaps useful trait of a scrapper lies in its saliva. These creatures produce copious amounts of it, and while it dries quite fast, it has powerful antiseptic qualities, which allows the creatures to eat even rotten, diseased or otherwise spoiled food. While not incredibly intelligent, domesticated scrappers have an instinct for licking wounds of its owners, staving off infection and sometimes even preventing them from contracting a dangerous illness. Scrappers have long, flexible spines and clean themselves in the same manner as cats do, using their saliva to treat both filthy fur and fresh wounds they acquire themselves, which may be the reason for their deep-seated instinct to help others in a similar way.

Scrappers are omnivores with robust stomachs and strong jaws, which allows them to eat and digest almost anything. In the wild, they subside on whatever they find. They often eat carrion too spoiled for other creatures and fruit from the trees that other animals have a hard time climbing, but can also subside on leaves, grass and roots when times are tough. As house pets, they gladly take care of any and all leftovers that they can get their little claws on. Due to the properties of their saliva, they are often allowed to lick clean both plates and cookware after their owners have eaten. These creatures are readily domesticated in rural areas and can easily fulfill similar tasks to cats and small dogs, which often amounts to protection from small, wild animals. While it is difficult, a scrapper can be trained for a hunt. The beast’s low stature and agility make it invaluable in hunts for burrow-dwelling creatures.

Scrappers don’t mate for life and rarely develop relationship with others of their kind, with rivalries being more common than friendships. The gestation period of a scrapper is close to 4 months and their litters are rarely larger than 3, which along with the audacity common to their kind means that the populations of these creatures are seldom fast-growing. An average scrapper is covered in dense fur, though it’s thinner in warmer climates. It has a great sense of smell and six clawed legs which allow them to both climb steep surfaces with incredible speed and agility and tear apart soon-to-be food. They are dense and muscular, very low to the ground and can reach two feet in length. Their hide is thick enough to occasionally stop a dog’s bite, and scrappers are more than willing to fight other animals, even those much larger than them, if threatened. While even wild scrappers are not hunters by nature, they never back down from challenges and don’t exhibit fear, which often ends badly for the creatures if they try their luck against a much stronger opponent.

Scrappers can be chosen as familiars by spellcasters with the Improved Familiar feat of any alignment and at least 3rd level.

At GM discretion, a scrapper can instead be taken as a standard familiar, in which case it grants its master a +2 bonus on Fortitude saves. Caution should be employed, as scrappers, while not overly strong, are much more powerful than most familiars.
